# Let people invite others to `<APP_NAME>` with roles

People work together in shared workspaces: an owner invites others by email
with a role, the invited person joins from the link (signing up if they have
no account), and each role decides what its members may see and do. Owners
manage members, change roles and withdraw invitations, and nobody reaches
another workspace's records.

## When to propose it

- "Invite my team", "add users", "share it with colleagues", "my staff need
  access".
- "Admins and members", "roles", "permissions", "read-only users".
- "Teams", "organisations", "companies", "clubs" sharing the same records.

## How to answer the person

Propose the simple way first: "People get workspaces. Whoever creates one owns
it and invites others by email, choosing a role for each; invited people join
from the link. JSKIT already has the members page, the invitation page and the
role checks, so we choose the roles and what each may do, and move your
records into workspaces."

Then say: "There are other options if you want to discuss." They are sharing
single records with named people instead of whole workspaces (no workspace
machinery when one owner per record is enough), signing in through an
organisation's own identity provider
([Sign in through an OIDC issuer](/guide/app-setup/sign-in-through-oidc-issuer)),
and one sign-in shared by several apps
([Run an accounts hub](/guide/app-setup/run-an-accounts-hub)).

## Product decisions (defaults)

- Tenancy: `tenancyMode: "workspaces"` with a personal workspace for people
  who came on their own (`autoProvision: "unless-member"`) and
  `allowSelfCreate: true`; an invited person joins the inviting workspace
  instead.
- Roles: `owner` (everything, never assignable), `admin` (members, invitations
  and settings), `member` (the app's records), each with a display `label`;
  the default invitation role is `member`.
- Only the invited address may accept, unless the person asks for any signed-in
  account holding the link.
- Invitations last 7 days; the owner can withdraw one.
- Outside production invitation email is logged and the inviter copies the
  link; production sends it through the app's email provider.
- Existing records move into their owner's personal workspace.

## Make a careful saved plan first

Write a careful saved plan first, then implement it item by item, proving each
one:

1. Set `tenancyMode` and `tenancyPolicy` in `config/public.js` after reading
   [Decide the tenancy model first](/guide/app-setup/multi-homing#decide-the-tenancy-model-first),
   and the two server settings the server refuses to start without,
   `config.workspaceSettings.defaults.invitesEnabled` and
   `config.workspaceMembers.defaults.inviteExpiresInMs`, in `config/server.js`
   ([Server composition](/guide/app-setup/multi-homing#server-composition)).
2. Install `@jskit-ai/workspaces-web` and run `npm run db:migrate`.
3. Add the workspace surfaces and the `workspace_member` access policy from the
   [workspace surfaces pattern](/patterns/workspaces/workspace-surfaces).
4. Write the role catalog with permissions, labels, `customPermissions` and
   `workspace.defaultInviteRole`.
5. Give the app's tables workspace ownership, with an add-only migration that
   moves existing rows into their owner's workspace.
6. Make the app's features and routes workspace-scoped.
7. Provide the invitation mailer.
8. Gate controls in the browser by permission.
9. Seed the browser tests' workspaces and members.

## Technical details

- **Read first:** [Workspace tenancy](/guide/app-setup/multi-homing)
  completely, and the [workspace server pattern](/patterns/workspaces/workspace-server).
- **Surfaces:** workspace pages live under `pagesRoot: "w/[workspaceSlug]"`
  with `requiresWorkspace: true`, administration under
  `w/[workspaceSlug]/admin`; the default surface stays free of a workspace so
  `/` and `/invite/:token` work
  ([Surfaces and where / lands](/guide/app-setup/multi-homing#surfaces-and-where-lands)).
  The **Your workspaces** page is `WorkspacesClientElement` from
  `@jskit-ai/workspaces-web/client/components/WorkspacesClientElement`.
- **Roles:** `roleCatalog.roles.<id>.permissions` grant `crud.<namespace>.*`
  operations, the workspace actions (`workspace.members.invite`,
  `workspace.members.manage`, `workspace.invites.revoke`, ...) and the app's own
  permissions listed in `roleCatalog.customPermissions`. A grant nothing
  requires stops the server in development and test
  ([Role permissions](/guide/app-setup/multi-homing#role-permissions)); labels
  go in `label` ([Role display labels](/guide/app-setup/multi-homing#role-display-labels)).
- **Data:** each table resource takes `ownership: "workspace"` (or
  `workspace_user` for a member's own rows); the handle stamps and scopes
  every statement from the request's context, never from input
  ([Layer 1](/guide/framework/data-access#layer-1-the-table-resource)). Jobs
  across workspaces use `systemContext(reason).forWorkspace(id)` and
  `workspaces.listForSystem`
  ([Background work](/guide/framework/data-access#background-work)).
- **Features and routes:** as
  [Workspace-scoped features and routes](/guide/app-setup/multi-homing#workspace-scoped-features-and-routes)
  shows; a route's `permission` is checked on the server, always.
- **Invitations:** who may accept is `config.workspaceInvitations`
  (`anyAccount`) and each workspace's `invitesRequireSameEmail`
  ([Who may accept an invitation](/guide/app-setup/multi-homing#who-may-accept-an-invitation)).
  Email goes through a `workspaces.invite-mailer` capability the app provides;
  JSKIT has no mail transport, so the mailer is the app's own (its email
  provider's client), and JSKIT applies `APP_ENV` to it: outside production
  the panel reports `simulated` and shows the link to copy
  ([Invitation email](/guide/app-setup/multi-homing#invitation-email)). A
  custom template is the `workspaces.invite-email-template` capability.
- **Browser:** a command names its permission with
  `useCommand({ runPermissions })` and the control hides or disables from
  `canRun`; the server still refuses.
- **Development sign-in** runs no provisioning: seed the workspaces and
  memberships the browser tests use
  ([Development sign-in](/guide/app-setup/multi-homing#development-sign-in)).

## Proof

Prove each behaviour at the cheapest level, never against development data
and never through a real email service.

- **Server tests** (`jskit test`, on `TEST_DB_NAME`, through `app.inject`):
  each role boundary (an action allowed and refused per role); another
  workspace's records unseen and unchanged with `expectScoped()`; a slug the
  caller is not in answers 404; invitation accept, refuse, expiry, withdrawal
  and the wrong address (403 `workspaces.invite.emailMismatchUser`); the
  mailer called in production with a fake transport and logged elsewhere.
- **Migration test:** existing rows land in their owner's workspace.
- **Browser tests** (`npm run test:e2e`): invite by email with a role, open the
  link as the invited person, join, see the shared records; a member without
  permission sees no invite control; switching workspaces keeps each one's
  records apart; at 390 and 1280 px.

## Leftovers for the person

- The email provider account and sending domain for production invitations.
- Real invitations sent to real inboxes on staging or production.
